transcript.text: my samsung washer dryer is making evrything smell damp/musty even after its washed, its gross. wot do i do

This is most often a build-up of detergent residue and bacteria in the door-seal folds, detergent drawer, filter and drum—not usually a failed part. A drain smell can also transfer to washing, while laundry that remains slightly damp after drying can soon smell musty. 1. Switch off and unplug the machine. Pull back the rubber door-seal folds and wipe out any slime, water or black mould. Clean the detergent drawer too. Visible residue or mould points to the usual hygiene build-up.
2. With towels and a shallow tray ready, open the lower filter flap and loosen the pump filter slowly. Remove fluff, hair and debris, then refit it securely. A blocked filter can hold stagnant water.
3. Run an empty 60–90°C maintenance wash with a washing-machine cleaner or soda crystals, following the product instructions. Do not put washing in for this cycle.
4. Afterwards, leave both the door and detergent drawer slightly ajar between washes, and avoid routinely using only cool washes or excessive detergent. If the smell is sharp, sulphur/rotten-egg-like and strongest by the drain hose or sink/standpipe, the likely issue is the waste plumbing or drain-hose setup rather than the washer-dryer itself. If it is hot, acrid, rubbery or electrical rather than musty, stop using it and unplug it—this needs fault diagnosis rather than cleaning. Is the smell earthy/musty, or more like drains/rotten eggs—and is it strongest from the laundry, the door seal/drawer, or near the drain hose?
its a damp musty smell, not eggy or drainy. strongest from the drum and the drawer when i open them. the standpipe doesnt smell of drains either

That points very strongly to a hygiene build-up inside the washer-dryer, rather than a drain or plumbing problem. The dispenser drawer area and drum are common places for detergent film and bacteria to sit, especially if the machine is usually shut after use or mainly used on cooler washes. Build on the cleaning steps already given by paying particular attention to the drawer housing: remove the drawer, clean the underside and the cavity it slides into with a cloth or small brush, then dry it. Also wipe the door seal folds dry after cleaning rather than just rinsing them. For future washes, use the stated detergent dose for your water hardness and load—too much detergent leaves a film that feeds the smell. If the smell returns immediately after this thorough clean, or there is persistent black mould embedded in a damaged door seal, the seal may need inspection or replacement. Otherwise this is normally cured by the clean and occasional hot maintenance wash, not by replacing a machine part.

candidates: Musty/mouldy biofilm or detergent residue in the door seal, drawer, filter or drum (high)
Drain odour from the waste plumbing or drain-hose arrangement (medium)
Drying load or drying performance leaving laundry damp (low)
